title: 9 Ways To Have More Authority Next School Year https://smartclassroommanagement.com/2017/07/22/9-ways-to-have-more-authority-next-school-year/
author: Michael Linsin
summary: Michael Linsin lays out nine concrete, learnable traits that build classroom authority, arguing that what appears to be an innate leadership gift is actually a teachable set of habits. The traits include dressing neatly, standing with confident posture, faithfully following through on promises, being honest rather than manipulative in praise and feedback, staying pleasant rather than intimidating, remaining calm under pressure, speaking concisely rather than rambling, staying physically well-rested and prepared, and consistently choosing to see the best in students and situations. He connects each trait to concrete effects — for example, citing research that posture alone can increase feelings of confidence — and warns that traits like intimidation or over-talking actively damage authority even when they produce short-term compliance. Linsin closes by asserting that these traits, taken together, form the 'secret sauce' others mistake for natural charisma, but which is in fact available to any teacher willing to adopt them.
points: Classroom authority is presented as a learnable set of nine specific traits, not an innate gift reserved for naturally charismatic teachers.
Follow-through on promises is called out as the single biggest lever: consistent follow-through builds authority quickly, while broken promises erode it just as fast.
Confident posture alone can increase felt confidence, according to cited research, even when a teacher isn't genuinely feeling assured.
Intimidation tactics like glaring, scolding, and losing composure may produce short-term compliance but cost respect, authority, and long-term behavior.
Being well-rested, efficient with lesson planning, and physically prepared is framed as a prerequisite for sustained authority and likeability.
quotes: Although, at first glance, authority appears to be an inborn gift reserved for a lucky few, there is really no mystery at all.
This one is huge. Do what you say you’re going to do and over time your authority will skyrocket.
The appearance of confidence can have the same effect. According to research, simply changing your posture can make you feel more powerful and thus behave more confidently.
Lecturing, glaring, scolding, and losing your cool may frighten students into behaving in the short term, but the price is your respect, plummeting authority, and more and more misbehavior.
Nervous energy has a way of spreading throughout the classroom, infecting every inch. It causes excitability, inattentiveness, and a form of misbehavior that is very difficult to eliminate.
But the truth is, it’s nothing more than a set of traits available to anyone. They’re available to anyone willing to adopt them for themself and dare to be more than just another teacher.
